note_on_method: Counts, addresses, lighting and hours come from the City of Scottsdale's pickleball page, checked against each venue's own entry rather than against the page as a whole. Cost, the sharing rule and the peak-time statement come from each park's own page, which also carries a feature list corroborating the court count and naming the restrooms. Counties and postcodes come from an address resolver: the US Census geocoder at three venues, and OpenStreetMap at Ashler Hills Park, whose address the Census has no record of. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description:
Eight outdoor lighted pickleball courts at the far northern edge of Scottsdale, near the Cave Creek boundary. Open sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily, first come and first served, with no reservation possible, the same terms that apply at every pickleball court the City lists.

This is the least documented of Scottsdale's four published venues. The park's own page lists "8 lighted pickleball courts" among the park's features and says nothing further. It does not carry the paragraph the Cholla, Horizon and Thompson Peak pages carry, the one that states the courts are free, sets out the rotation rule and names mornings as the busiest time. So this venue publishes with no price, no sharing rule and no peak-time statement.
slots.getting_there:
32220 N. 74th Way, Scottsdale, AZ 85266, at the northern edge of the city. The postcode here comes from OpenStreetMap rather than from the US Census address geocoder that every other venue on this site uses, because the Census address file holds no record of this address at all. That is why this venue was excluded when Scottsdale was first published: a venue must have an address that resolves before it may appear here, and until 4 September 2026 this site had exactly one resolver.

The City's own page prints the address as "Scottsdale, AZ 32220", repeating the street number where the postcode belongs.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight lit courts, no booking and no stated price. The City's city-wide rules apply: first come, first served, no reservation required, and no amplified sound at any of its pickleball locations. The rotation rule published for the other three parks (standard game to 11, win by two, a 30-minute limit, rotate off for anyone waiting) is not stated for this park. Surface, nets and parking are not published.

faqs.a: Eight, and both City pages say so. The pickleball page reads "Eight outdoor lighted pickleball courts" and the park's own page lists "8 lighted pickleball courts" among its features.

Not verified. The City has published no price for this park either way. The other three Scottsdale venues carry the sentence "They are free to use" on their park pages; Ashler Hills' page has no equivalent sentence, so the cost is recorded as unverified rather than assumed.
Yes. The park page's feature list names restrooms, alongside a playground, a lighted basketball court, open turf play areas and walking paths.

slots.description: Eight outdoor lighted pickleball courts in east Scottsdale, free to use, drop-in and not reservable. What sets this venue apart from almost every other one in this directory is not the count but the documentation: the City of Scottsdale publishes not just how many courts there are but how to share them. Its page for Cholla states the rule in full: play is standard game format, first side to 11 points or leading by at least two, with a 30-minute time limit, at which point players "should rotate off the court with any waiting players". It then adds the sentence that no other operator in this directory has published anywhere: "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play at Cholla."
slots.getting_there: 11320 E. Via Linda, Scottsdale, AZ 85259, which the Census geocoder matched to Scottsdale city, Maricopa County. This is a suburban park below the McDowell Mountains rather than a street-grid site. The City publishes nothing about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Turn up, put your paddle in the queue, and expect to wait in the morning. The courts are lit and open from sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily. There is no booking system anywhere in Scottsdale, and no amplified sound is permitted at any of the City's pickleball locations. Games run to 11, win by two, and a 30-minute clock applies when people are waiting. Nothing is published about the surface or about nets. Restrooms are in the feature list on the park's own page, and the City states plainly that the courts are free to use.

faqs.a: Eight. The City's pickleball page lists "Eight outdoor lighted courts" and the park's own page confirms it: "There are eight pickleball courts at Cholla Park, which are available for drop in public use and are not reservable."
Yes, and the City writes it down: "They are free to use."

faqs.q: When should I arrive to get on?
faqs.a: Not in the morning, if you can avoid it. The City states that mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play here. It is the only operator in this directory to have published a peak time at all, so this is the rare case where that advice is sourced rather than guessed.
Not verified. Scottsdale states no surface at any of its venues.

slots.description:
Ten outdoor lighted pickleball courts, the largest count in Scottsdale, and one of the larger single-site counts anywhere in this directory. Free to use, drop-in, not reservable, open sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily. Horizon Park sits in north-east Scottsdale off 100th Street, and the City publishes the rule for sharing a court alongside the count: standard game to 11, win by two, a 30-minute limit, then rotate off for whoever is waiting.

Ten courts changes what a busy session feels like. At a two-court venue a queue is a wait; at ten it is a rotation, and the City's 30-minute clock is what makes that work. The City also states that mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play here.
slots.getting_there: 15444 N. 100th St., Scottsdale, AZ 85260, matched by the Census geocoder to Scottsdale city, Maricopa County. Cholla Park's eight courts are a few miles away, the nearest published alternative. Nothing is published about parking at any Scottsdale venue.
slots.what_to_expect: The best odds in Scottsdale of getting on a court, and the same rules as everywhere else in the city: no booking, first come first served, games to 11 with a 30-minute limit when people are waiting, no amplified sound. Lit until 10:30 p.m., which in a Phoenix-area summer is the whole basis on which the venue is usable. Surface and nets are not published. Restrooms are, in the park page's feature list, and so is the price, which is nothing.

faqs.a: Ten: "10 outdoor lighted courts" on the City's pickleball page, and "There are ten pickleball courts at Horizon Park" on the park's own page. It is the largest count in the city.
Yes. The park page states "They are free to use".

Mornings. The City states "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play at Horizon" on the park's own page — one of only three venues in this entire directory where a peak time has been published by the operator, and all three are in Scottsdale.

faqs.q: Can I book for a group?
faqs.a: No. The City's pickleball page states that no reservation is required and courts are first come, first served. For a group, the practical approach is the City's own rotation rule: games to 11, win by two, 30-minute limit, rotate off for waiting players.

slots.description:
Three outdoor lighted pickleball courts with three portable nets in north Scottsdale, and closed at the time this page was last checked. The City states that all pickleball courts at Thompson Peak Park were shut from Monday 17 August to Friday 11 September 2026 for resurfacing, and are expected to reopen on Saturday 12 September, weather permitting. The page was checked on 4 September, inside that window.

When open, it is the smallest of Scottsdale's four published venues and carries the same terms as Cholla and Horizon: free to use, drop-in, not reservable, open sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily, with the City's rotation rule (standard game to 11, win by two, 30-minute limit, rotate off for waiting players) and the same statement that mornings are typically busiest. The park also has an inclusive playground the City describes at length.
slots.getting_there: 20199 N. 78th Pl., Scottsdale, AZ 85255, matched by the Census geocoder to Scottsdale city, Maricopa County. The park's own page prints its postcode as "Scottsdale, AZ 20199", the street number in the postcode's place. The City's pickleball page has it right, and the postcode published here comes from the geocoder. Ashler Hills Park's page carries the same fault.
slots.what_to_expect: First, check whether it has reopened. After that: three lit courts, free, no booking, and three portable nets that the City lists as a feature of the venue without saying who sets them up, so bring one if you have one. The courts were shut for resurfacing, so whenever they reopen the surface will be new. Mornings are the busiest time, per the City.

faqs.a: It was closed when checked on 4 September 2026. The City states the courts were closed from 17 August to 11 September for resurfacing and expected to reopen on Saturday 12 September, weather permitting.

Three, plus three portable nets which the City lists alongside them. The pickleball page reads "Three outdoor lighted courts / Three portable nets", and the park page confirms "There are three pickleball courts at Thompson Peak Park".

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Not verified. The City lists three portable nets as a feature of the venue but never says whether they are provided for public use or who sets them up. Bring one if you have one.
Yes: "They are free to use", per the park's own page, the same as at Cholla and Horizon.
